Best Rugged Tablets for Plumbers and Heating Engineers

13 October 2026 Tuga Hardware

For most plumbers and heating engineers, the Tuga A8 at £379 is the one to start with. It is an 8 inch Android tablet with IP67 sealing, a removable 8000mAh battery, a camera flash and a 1000 nit screen big enough for commissioning forms and quotes. If you want something that lives in a pocket instead, the Tuga A6 at £349 is a 6 inch IP67 handheld with a camera flash for the dark spaces this trade works in. If a boiler manufacturer's service software only runs on a Windows PC, the Tuga W8 at £629 is the Windows option to look at.

What Plumbing and Heating Work Does to a Device

This trade is hard on electronics in ordinary ways. Your hands are wet for much of the day. The device goes down on a tiled floor, a worktop beside a running tap, or the bottom of a bath you are fitting. It picks up flux, jointing compound and boiler dust, and lives under sinks, in airing cupboards and lofts, and on a van dashboard in January.

A consumer phone in a case can handle the paperwork: commissioning checklists, service records, landlord certificates, photos, a quote at the kitchen table and a signature before you go. It is the water, the drops and the dark cupboards that finish it off. So the shortlist comes down to sealing, a camera that works in poor light, a battery that lasts a day of callouts, and an operating system that runs your software. Start with the software.

Three Questions Before You Look at Specs

1. Does Any of Your Software Need Windows?

Boiler manufacturers can offer two kinds of software. The first is a phone app for commissioning, fault codes and service reminders, which may talk to the boiler over Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. Apps like that are often written for phones. Check with the manufacturer that the app supports the Android version on the device (Android 15 on the A6, Android 12 on the A8), then try it on the device before you rely on it. Android 12 is an older release than the A6's Android 15, so a newer app is more likely to leave it behind. Check the A8 with extra care.

The second kind is diagnostic or service software that installs on a Windows PC and connects to the boiler through an interface lead. If your work involves that, you need a Windows device. Check with the manufacturer which platforms the software supports, whether it needs a specific interface, and whether it runs on Windows 11. Do not take a retailer's word for it, including ours.

If your flue gas analyser has a companion app for logging readings and producing the customer's report, check the analyser manufacturer's list of supported devices and Android versions. If you print to a separate printer, check that pairs too.

Our Android or Windows guide has a five minute test for this. One Windows only program you cannot do without means Windows. Everything else means Android, which is cheaper, lighter and, on the tablets, has bigger batteries.

2. How Wet Does It Get?

IP67 and IP68 are dust tight and rated for immersion, a metre for 30 minutes on IP67 and deeper on IP68. IP65 is dust tight and protected against water jets, but not immersion. Our IP68 vs IP67 guide explains the ratings in full. For this trade: IP67 and IP68 are rated for immersion, so a drop into a bath is within the rating. IP65 is not rated for immersion.

One more rating matters here. IP69K covers high pressure, high temperature water jets, which is what lets a device survive jet washing. No device in our range carries it, so wipe them clean rather than hosing them down.

3. Handheld or Tablet?

Then decide between a handheld and a tablet. A handheld lives in a pocket or holster and comes out many times a day for a photo or a fault code. A tablet lives in the van and comes into the house for a quote or a long form. Some firms run both.

Tuga A6: The One for the Toolbag

The Tuga A6 is the pocket option, and at £349 it is the lowest priced device in our range.

  • 6 inch FHD+ IPS screen, 2160 x 1080
  • IP67, rated for 1.5 metre drops
  • 13MP rear camera with flash, 5MP front
  • 5050mAh removable battery
  • 4G LTE dual SIM, dual-band Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.1, NFC
  • Built-in 2D barcode scanner with two side scan keys
  • Android 15, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, microSD up to 256GB
  • 277g, rated for -20°C to 50°C
  • £349

Pocket size is the reason to pick it over the A8 for this trade. At 277g it comes out under a sink, behind a boiler casing, in a cylinder cupboard or across a loft for a quick photo, and the flash helps where a torch would need the hand that is holding the device. Before and after shots, data plates, the state of a flue, the leak you want the customer to see. The barcode scanner is useful if you log parts or van stock.

IP67 means a drop into a bath is within the rating, though it is not rated for jet washing. The A6 does not list glove mode, a fingerprint sensor or face unlock, so set a PIN. The 5050mAh battery is smaller than the A8's 8000mAh, but like the A8's it is removable, so a charged spare can take over mid shift. The Belt Holster (£22), Car Phone Mount (£17) and 12V DC Car Charger (£26) fit it.

Where it falls short: it is a phone sized screen with a smaller battery. A long commissioning form, or a quote with options at the kitchen table, is cramped on 6 inches.

Tuga A8: The Van Tablet

The Tuga A8 is an 8 inch Android tablet built to live in the van and come into the house for the paperwork.

  • 8 inch IPS screen with AGC glass, 1280 x 800, 1000 nits
  • IP67
  • 8000mAh removable battery
  • 4G LTE dual SIM, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC
  • 13MP autofocus rear camera with flash, 5MP front
  • Android 12, 6GB RAM, 128GB storage, microSD slot
  • VESA mount points and pogo pin contacts; USB-C and DC in
  • £379

Eight inches is enough for a form with a lot of fields, a system drawing or a quote with pictures, and it still fits a van door pocket. The 1000 nit screen is readable in bright light, which matters on a roof or at an external boiler or heat pump unit. The camera has a flash, which helps in an airing cupboard or a loft. VESA mount points on the back mean the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109), a locking VESA mount with DC power input, bolts to a dashboard or windscreen and keeps the A8 secure and powered on the road. The same manufacturer check on apps applies as for the A6, and matters more here because Android 12 is the oldest Android version in our range.

Where it differs from the A6: the same IP67 sealing, a bigger screen at 1000 nits, a larger removable battery, 6GB RAM rather than 4GB, and VESA docking. Against that, there is no barcode scanner, it runs Android 12 rather than Android 15, and no drop rating, weight or operating temperature is listed for it, where the A6 lists 1.5 metre drops, 277g and -20°C to 50°C. It costs £30 more, and it is the better choice when the screen does more work than your pocket.

Tuga W8: When the Software Only Runs on a PC

The Tuga W8 is an 8 inch Windows 11 Pro tablet. It exists in this trade for one reason: the boiler or controls software you need is a Windows program.

  • Windows 11 Pro on an Intel Celeron N5100, 8GB RAM, 128GB SSD
  • 8 inch screen, 1920 x 1200, 550 nits
  • IP65, MIL-STD-810G, 1.22m drops
  • Removable 5000mAh battery with PD fast charge
  • 4G LTE, Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.0, GPS and GLONASS, NFC
  • USB-C, USB-A and Mini HDMI, pogo pin dock connector
  • 8MP rear camera plus 5MP front
  • 910g, rated for -20°C to 60°C
  • £629

It runs Windows 11 Pro and has USB-C, USB-A and Mini HDMI ports. Whether your manufacturer's software installs and runs on it, and which connector its interface lead needs, is for the manufacturer to confirm before you buy. Also confirm that the software runs on Windows 11, that the interface has a current driver, and that it is usable with a touchscreen rather than a mouse.

IP65 covers dust and water jets, not a drop into a bath or a bucket, and there is no IP69K, so keep it out of standing water and do not hose it down or pressure wash it. If your work is wet, the IP67 A6 and A8 are the safer choice. The 5000mAh battery is well short of the A8's 8000mAh and about the same as the A6's, but it is removable, so a charged spare can take over, and you can plan on the 12V DC Car Charger (£26) between jobs or the Charging Dock (£49.99) at base. It is rated for -20°C to 60°C, against -20°C to 50°C for the A6 (no operating temperature is listed for the A8), and its military standard rating is MIL-STD-810G, the older revision rather than 810H.

The W8 is £280 more than the A6 and £250 more than the A8. If the only Windows program in your week could run on the office PC after the job, buy Android and keep the difference. If it is needed on site every week and the manufacturer confirms it runs on Windows 11, the W8 earns its keep.

What About the W10 and WH6?

The Tuga W10 (£649) adds a 10.1 inch screen, an Intel N100 and a wired Ethernet port, but it weighs 1197g against the W8's 910g, so it suits commercial heating and controls work rather than domestic wet work. The Tuga WH6 (£699) is Windows 11 in a 6.5 inch handheld. Like the W8, both are IP65 and none of the three is rated for immersion.

Winter Callouts

The A6 and the W8 are both rated to operate down to -20°C. No operating temperature is listed for the A8, so if you work through hard frosts, weigh that up. Do not put a frozen device straight onto a charger, and let it warm up and dry off before you plug it in. Our winter battery guide explains why.

Buying as a Small Firm

Every device includes a 12 month warranty against defects in materials and workmanship. The paid 3-Year Warranty is offered on every model: £65 on the A6, A8 and A10, £79 on the W8 and W10, and £89 on the WH6. Delivery is free to UK addresses and takes 7 to 10 working days. Prices are what you pay. No VAT to add.

If you are equipping more than one engineer, our bulk orders page covers volume pricing, and any UK registered business, sole traders included, can apply for a trade account. For a quote or a proforma invoice, contact us with the models and quantities.

Which One to Buy

  • Domestic plumbing and heating, apps and web based paperwork: Tuga A8, £379.
  • The same, but you want it in a pocket, not the van: Tuga A6, £349.
  • A Windows only diagnostic or service program you use on site: Tuga W8, £629, if you can keep it out of standing water.
  • Commercial plant and controls, plugging into panels: Tuga W10, £649, if you can keep it out of standing water.

Whatever you choose, do the software check first. List the boiler apps, the analyser app and the job management system you use, confirm with each maker that it runs on the device, then compare hardware. A device that cannot run your analyser app is no use at any price.
